# PVM: handle invalid instructions

## Pull Request by @mateuszsikora

# What ?
This PR changes PVM behaviour in case of invalid instruction. Previously it throw an error, now it is correctly handled.

In GP we have:
[<img width="648" alt="Screenshot 2024-08-07 at 09 52 43" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5da3a3a4-c00e-4fde-8a95-92bf77e09ce4">](https://graypaper.fluffylabs.dev/#)

(Please note that this image is clickable and it would be nice if our GP Reader is able to generate such ready to paste markdown code)

We have two options to handle an invalid instruction:
1. change status to panic and quit program immediately 
2. treat the invalid instruction as regular `trap`

The difference is that in the second case we don't need any additional condition and gas will be subtracted automagically so I've chosen this option.


## Comment by @mateuszsikora

> While the change is good, I'd love to actually see the link to the tool directly in the code with the same explanation as you gave in the PR description.

I can place it in the code as well but be aware of the link length :D - are you sure you want to keep it in the code? :D


> I'm also wondering if we should even start executing programs with invalid instructions. Obviously there is a case, when these invalid instructions are never reached, however since the bytecode is clearly defined the only reason I see to actually start executing an invalid program is to avoid this linear traversal over instruction mask. But IMHO it's a bit of a moot point - we already know exactly where to look so it should be trivial to reject such programs.
> 
> Did you see anything that the gray paper says about that? If not we should maybe start a discussion in the GP channel?


There is no information in GP that you should validate a program at the beginning. Rather in corner cases you have additional condition that should cause the panic result so my understanding of that is: we should execute incorrect programs until we detect some problem
